name: Disorder of Lipid Absorption and Transport

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Lipid Absorption and Transport Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of chronic steatorrhea confirmed by fecal fat analysis
Marked hypocholesterolemia with low plasma lipid levels
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in lipid absorption or transport
Symptoms consistent with lipid malabsorption such as failure to thrive or fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies
Improvement with dietary fat restriction and supplementation of fat-soluble vitamins

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic steatorrhea, hypocholesterolemia, and confirmatory genetic testing
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis may be supported by clinical presentation and response to treatment but requires major criteria.

pathognomonic.notes: Persistent fatty stools due to malabsorption

common.symptomName: Fat-soluble vitamin deficiencies (A, D, E, K)
common.notes: Manifesting as night blindness, osteomalacia, neuropathy, or coagulopathy
searchTerms: lack of vitamins A, D, E, K

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive in infancy or childhood
common.notes: Poor weight gain and growth delay
searchTerms: poor growth and development in early life
failure to thrive in babies or children

common.notes: Due to malabsorption and intestinal dysfunction

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness secondary to vitamin E deficiency
searchTerms: muscle weakness from vitamin E lack
weak muscles due to vitamin deficiency
low vitamin E causing muscle fatigue

occasional.symptomName: Coagulopathy due to vitamin K deficiency
searchTerms: bleeding problems from vitamin K lack
blood clotting issues due to vitamin deficiency
coagulopathy linked to vitamin K shortage

occasional.notes: Dry, scaly skin due to vitamin A deficiency

rare.symptomName: Cardiomyopathy related to lipid metabolism abnormalities
searchTerms: heart muscle disease from fat metabolism problems
cardiac issues due to lipid imbalance
heart weakness linked to fat processing

laboratory: Fecal fat quantification showing increased fat excretion
Low plasma cholesterol and triglyceride levels
Reduced serum levels of fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K
Prolonged prothrombin time due to vitamin K deficiency
imaging: Abdominal ultrasound may show fatty infiltration of liver
Bone density scans indicating osteopenia or osteoporosis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes involved in lipid absorption and transport such as MTTP, APOB, SAR1B
other: Improvement of symptoms with dietary fat restriction and vitamin supplementation

distinguishingFeatures: Milder clinical course compared to other lipid absorption disorders

redFlags: Persistent steatorrhea with failure to thrive
Severe hypocholesterolemia unresponsive to dietary changes
Neurological deterioration due to vitamin E deficiency
